blogs.title: The Pulmonary Masquerade: Recurrent Bloody Pleural Effusions That Aren’t Thoracic
blogs.description: Walk through a pragmatic diagnostic approach to recurrent, hemorrhagic pleural effusion in children. Emphasize early addition of pleural fluid amylase/lipase to the workup, key differentials (PPF, esophageal perforation, malignancy, TB), and pattern recognition (large unilateral effusions, rapid reaccumulation, minimal fever). Provide a stepwise algorithm to avoid anchoring on thoracic causes and shorten time to identifying pancreatic sources.

blogs.title: Handlebar Pancreas to Hemithorax: How Traumatic Pancreatitis Becomes a Pancreatopleural Fistula
blogs.description: Explain the pathophysiology of PPF after blunt abdominal trauma: duct disruption/pseudocyst, retroperitoneal tracking via the esophageal/aortic hiatus, and eventual pleural entry. Discuss right- vs left-sided effusions, bilateral communications, and why respiratory symptoms dominate in kids. Include pearls on eliciting late or concealed trauma histories and why obesity and diet may modulate pancreatitis risk/severity.

blogs.title: Imaging PPF in Kids: CXR and POCUS to CT, MRCP, then ERCP
blogs.description: Outline an imaging-first strategy for suspected PPF that balances diagnostic yield and radiation. Cover: CXR/POCUS for triage and drainage guidance; CT for complications and collections (but limited fistula visualization); MRCP for fistula/ductal anatomy (70–80% sensitivity); and ERCP as the therapeutic gold standard. Include when to image before chest tube placement, and practical tips for coordinating MRCP and ERCP in pediatrics.

blogs.title: Treating Pancreatopleural Fistula: A Practical Pediatric Algorithm
blogs.description: Provide a bedside algorithm for management: initial stabilization and pleural drainage (thoracentesis vs ICD), bowel rest, TPN, octreotide dosing (10–40 µg/kg/day; case used 30 µg/kg/day), and PERT. Define success/failure windows (2–3 weeks), indications for ERCP with transpapillary stenting (ductal stenosis/pressure relief), and when to consider surgery (distal pancreatectomy, Puestow, cystojejunostomy). Summarize reported success rates and timelines to set expectations for families and teams.

blogs.title: TB Trap: Interpreting Pleural ADA and TB Contact in the Era of PPF
blogs.description: Discuss the diagnostic pitfall of mildly elevated pleural ADA and positive TB contact leading to empiric anti-TB therapy in non-TB effusions. Review ADA thresholds, pretest probability, and confirmatory testing (GeneXpert, culture, histology). Contrast with PPF clues: massive recurrent effusions, bloody fluid, very high amylase/lipase, and negative infectious markers. Offer a checklist to prevent premature TB treatment when PPF is on the table.

blogs.title: Lab Pearls: Ordering and Interpreting Pleural Fluid Amylase (Pancreatic vs Salivary)
blogs.description: Detail when and how to order pleural fluid amylase/lipase and isoenzyme typing. Clarify that levels ≥1000 IU/L suggest PPF, but elevated amylase can also occur in esophageal perforation and malignancy—typically salivary-type amylase. Provide tips on specimen handling, coordinating concurrent serum testing, and integrating results with clinical/imaging data to refine the differential.
